comments.author: @MarkLKahnt
comments.text:
The original “districts” of the NorthWest Territories were horizontal, with the move to the current vertical orientations when the provinces were created and joined Confederation. Up until the Great Depression, Saskatchewan dominated western Canada, while Alberta was comparable to Manitoba and British Columbia was smaller than any of the three, lacking much flat land on which to settle. The dust bowl hit Saskatchewan very hard (look up Bennett Buggies) and growth stalled. Alberta actually suffered more due to some funny money policies, only eventually bailed out by oil, which led the Albertan political class to decide that they just knew better than anyone else how to do things. 

Saskatchewan never recovered, now having the smallest population of the four western provinces and sixth overall, while Alberta is the second largest western province (BC is bigger) and fourth overall. Ontario is first nationally, with Québec second. Both William Lyon Mackenzie King and John Diefenbaker represented Prince Albert, Saskatchewan as Prime Minister, while four of the two dozen Prime Ministers have strong Albertan connections, three representing seats there (although Joe Clark was the only one born in the province) and Mark Carney was raised in Alberta, although he was born in the NorthWest Territories. 

The two provinces also have different philosophies - a deeply ingrained cooperative attitude in Saskatchewan, while Alberta is much more individualistic.
